reasons: narrow: The original assertion that the exponents can be made arbitrarily large by increasing \(C\) omits that the same enlargement can violate sparse occupancy. Under the frozen profile definition \(v\asymp\ell^d\), so \(nv\le c_0\) is equivalent up to fixed constants to \(n\delta^{d/q}\le c_*\); the factor \(h^d\ell^d\) belongs to \(kp_2/n^2\), not to one-cell occupancy. The proposed claim restricts the separation guarantee to compatible multipliers, derives the requested lower bound \(\epsilon\gtrsim C^{D_F}n^{-1+q/d+q/\gamma}\), identifies the exact boundary \(d\ge2q+qd/\gamma\), and states that dense occupancy requires a new argument.

verdict.note: Accepted after independent algebra audit: exact sparse-occupancy domain and dense-occupancy elbow are faithful, and all exponents/boundaries check.
